                "headline": "Special Weather Statement issued September 12 at 1:12PM CDT by NWS New Orleans LA",
                "description": "At 112 PM CDT, Doppler radar was tracking an area of strong\nthunderstorms capable of producing funnel clouds over Paradis, or 7\nmiles southwest of Hahnville, moving northeast at 5 mph.\n\nHAZARD...Wind gusts up to 40 mph and funnel clouds.\n\nSOURCE...Radar indicated.\n\nIMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around\nunsecured objects.\n\nLocations impacted include...\nHahnville, Laplace, Paradis, Boutte, Bayou Gauche, Des Allemands,\nTaft, Luling, Killona, Destrehan, Norco, Montz and Edgard.",
                "instruction": "Conditions are favorable for the development of weak, brief funnel\nclouds. This type of funnel cloud is harmless, but on rare occasions\nthey can briefly touch down, producing wind gusts over 50 mph. If a\nfunnel cloud is spotted move indoors or to safe harbor and report\nyour sighting to the National Weather Service.\n\nFrequent cloud to ground lightning is occurring with this storm.\nLightning can strike 10 miles away from a thunderstorm.                 "senderName": "NWS Raleigh NC",
                "headline": "Flood Advisory issued September 12 at 2:11PM EDT until September 12 at 3:45PM EDT by NWS Raleigh NC",
                "description": "* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.\n\n* WHERE...Southeastern Durham County and Wake County in central North\nCarolina...\n\n* WHEN...Until 345 PM EDT.\n\n* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- At 209 PM EDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to\nthunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin\nshortly in the advisory area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain have\nfallen. The heaviest rain has occurred in northeast Cary in the\nCrossroads area, and in northwest Raleigh near New Hope.\n- This includes the following streams and drainages...\nReedy Creek, Rocky Branch, Crabtree Creek, Walnut Creek, Neuse\nRiver.\n\nAdditional rainfall amounts of 1 to 1.5 inches are expected over\nthe area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.\n- Some locations that will experience flooding include...\nRaleigh, Durham, Cary, Garner, RDU International, Apex,\nMorrisville, Knightdale, William B Umstead State Park, Lake\nWheeler, Research Triangle, Falls Lake Boat Ramp, Lake Benson,\nCarpenter, Bethesda and Parkwood.\n- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood",

                "description": "SMWSJU\n\nThe National Weather Service in San Juan has issued a\n\n* Special Marine Warning for...\nMona Passage Southward to 17N...\nCoastal Waters of Northwestern Puerto Rico out 10 NM...\nCoastal Waters of Southwestern Puerto Rico out 10 NM...\n\n* Until 245 PM AST.\n\n* At 210 PM AST, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing\nwaterspouts was located just offshore northern Cabo Rojo and\nMayaguez, moving west at 5 knots.\n\nHAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts to 34 knots.\n\nSOURCE...Radar indicated.\n\nIMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally\nhazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly\nhigher winds and suddenly higher waves.\n\n* Locations impacted include...\nMainly open waters of Mona Passage Southward to 17N, Coastal Waters\nof Northwestern Puerto Rico out 10 NM and Coastal Waters of\nSouthwestern Puerto Rico out 10 NM.",

                "headline": "Special Weather Statement issued September 12 at 2:07PM EDT by NWS Charleston WV",
                "description": "At 207 PM EDT, Doppler radar was tracking a cluster of strong\nthunderstorms near Rio Grande, moving northeast at 30 mph.\n\nHAZARD...Pea size hail.\n\nSOURCE...Radar indicated.\n\nIMPACT...Minor hail damage to vegetation is possible.\n\nLocations impacted include...\nPoint Pleasant, Gallipolis, Pomeroy, Rio Grande, Racine, Rutland, New\nHaven, Mason, Middleport, Syracuse, Hartford City, Henderson,\nCheshire, Adamsville, Lakin, Letart, and Kyger.",
                "instruction": "If outdoors, consider seeking shelter inside a building.\n\nTorrential rainfall is also occurring with this storm and may lead to\nlocalized flooding.                 "description": "* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be\npossible.\n\n* WHERE...Portions of east central Ohio, including the following\nareas, Belmont, Carroll, Columbiana, Coshocton, Guernsey, Harrison,\nJefferson OH, Monroe, Muskingum, Noble and Tuscarawas,\nPennsylvania, including the following areas, Allegheny, Armstrong,\nBeaver, Butler, Clarion, Fayette, Forest, Greene, Higher Elevations\nof Fayette, Higher Elevations of Indiana, Higher Elevations of\nWestmoreland, Indiana, Jefferson PA, Lawrence, Mercer, Venango,\nWashington and Westmoreland, and West Virginia, including the\nfollowing areas, Brooke, Eastern Preston, Eastern Tucker, Hancock,\nMarion, Marshall, Monongalia, Ohio, Preston, Ridges of Eastern\nMonongalia and Northwestern Preston, Western Tucker and Wetzel.\n\n* WHEN...Through late tonight.\n\n* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,\ncreeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.\n\n* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...\n- Scattered thunderstorm development during the late morning and\nearly afternoon hours, followed by a more widespread push of\nheavy rain and additional thunderstorms, could result in a couple\nrounds of heavy rain.
